topic.title: Graph Clustering and Approximation Guarantees
topic.area: Graphical Models, Clustering, and Network Structure
topic.overview: Graph clustering groups nodes using edges that express similarity, disagreement, or constraints. This topic studies spectral methods, hierarchical and overlapping groups, correlation clustering, and scalable approximation algorithms. The graph representation and objective determine what a good partition means, so different formulations can legitimately produce different groupings.
topic.whyItMatters: Large graphs make exact optimization difficult, but worst-case hardness does not reveal how good a particular heuristic solution is. Instance-specific certificates can narrow that gap. Constraints such as group size or fairness further change the feasible solutions and the computational structure of the problem.
topic.evolution: A 1998 randomized method clusters pairwise similarities while addressing noisy edges. Later representatives develop spectral and near-linear approximation methods. A 2025 constrained approach uses signed Laplacians and generalized eigenvalues; 2026 work computes lower bounds that certify the quality of practical correlation-clustering and max-cut solutions on individual graphs.
openQuestions: How can clustering objectives reflect application constraints without making solutions opaque?
Which scalable certificates remain informative on sparse, noisy, or overlapping community structure?
